title: New repo setup has a repeatable process

brief.why: Every new repo is fumbled — inconsistent init, missing CLAUDE.md, no understanding.md seed, manual GitHub creation. Wastes the first 10 minutes of every new project.
brief.what: 1. Design the scaffold checklist 2. Build the skill 3. Wire it so /close can invoke it when scratch → new repo
brief.done: Running /scaffold in an empty directory produces a ready-to-work repo with bon, CLAUDE.md, and GitHub remote
brief.how:
A /scaffold skill in trousse following the skill-forge pattern: deterministic init script + LLM fill-in + deterministic validator.

The scaffold is the "compound step" for repo creation (cf. Every's compound engineering: Plan→Work→Review→Compound). Each repo we create teaches the system; the scaffold codifies that learning so future repos start from a higher baseline. It encodes our taste (hatchling, src layout, bon, CLAUDE.md) into a reproducible system rather than tribal knowledge.

Three invocation modes:
1. **Greenfield** — empty directory, everything from scratch
2. **Adopt** — working code exists (scratch/noodling), needs proper structure wrapped around it
3. **Extract** — pulling a module out of an existing repo into its own (what we did with deglacer from ccconv)

Architecture follows skill-forge's proven three-part split:
- `init_repo.py` (deterministic) — creates skeleton: git init, pyproject.toml, src layout, .gitignore, tests/, bon init, gh repo create. Leaves [TODO] markers.
- SKILL.md (LLM judgment) — interviews for name/purpose/mode, runs the script, fills in CLAUDE.md content (module map, conventions, quick commands), validates.
- `validate_repo.py` (deterministic) — checks structural conformance against the checklist.

The checklist (derived from deglacer + cross-repo survey of 10 batterie repos, April 2026):
- git init + main branch (never detached HEAD)
- .gitignore (Python standard)
- pyproject.toml: hatchling build backend, src/<pkg>/ layout, [dependency-groups] dev, [tool.pytest.ini_options] with pythonpath=["src"] and testpaths=["tests"]
- src/<pkg>/__init__.py with __version__ via importlib.metadata
- tests/ with __init__.py + conftest.py stub
- CLAUDE.md (orientation, quick commands, module map, key conventions)
- bon init --prefix <prefix>
- .bon/understanding.md seed
- gh repo create (public by default, HTTPS)
- First commit + push

Python-only for v1. TypeScript variant (package.json, tsconfig, vitest) is a future extension — don't build it, but don't prevent it either.

Invocation: Claude-suggestible, user-approved. /close can suggest it when detecting work in a non-repo directory. Never automatic.

title: Update trousse deglacer skill to wrap shared library

brief.why: After extracting core parsing into the deglacer package, trousse's ccconv/deglacer skill still has the old inline implementation. It should become a thin wrapper.

brief.done: Trousse's deglacer skill imports from shared library. No duplicate parsing code.
brief.how:
This action needs rethinking before execution. The original plan was "trousse wraps deglacer" but a better framing may be "deglacer owns the skill, trousse redirects."

Before touching code, investigate:
1. Read trousse's deglacer skill (skills/deglacer/SKILL.md) — what does it provide beyond ccconv invocation? Schema reference? Interactive exploration patterns? Those belong in deglacer if it's the canonical home.
2. Read gueridon's CC session handling — does it parse JSONL independently? If so, it's a fourth consumer to fold in (not tracked as a separate action yet).
3. Check garde-manger's claude_code adapter — how much of its own parsing does it have? (Informs whether gazuzi is a light rewire or heavy surgery.)

Then decide: does the skill move into deglacer (becoming a CC plugin with .claude-plugin/), or does it stay in trousse as a thin wrapper? Trade-offs:
- Moving it: deglacer becomes self-contained (library + skill + CLI + schema docs). But it gains plugin machinery and marketplace coupling.
- Keeping it in trousse: cleaner separation (library vs skill). But the schema reference and skill orchestration logic live apart from the parsing they describe.

Either way, ccconv.py in trousse should become a thin shim that imports from deglacer — no duplicate parsing code.
